flares.note: Simultaneous flaring from S20E19 and an unnumbered AR on the E limb around N06.
Manually selected start time at 2026-07-27T02:37Z via GOES-Pri X-ray flux timeline and SDO AIA 131. Manually calculated end time.

cmes.note: Faint CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only. No clear source candidate is observed in SDO AIA or GOES SUVI.

cmeAnalyses.note: This is a SOHO LASCO C2/C3 plane-of-sky measurement.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the WNW in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-07-21T06:23Z. It is also seen to the NW in SOH0 LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is largely obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. There is a larger shock feature that appears as a halo in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is most likely wide opening field lines seen near the W limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 beginning around 2026-07-21T05:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of brightest, densest part of the leading edge based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.
Shock front triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-21T07:48Z. It also seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the N in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is a filament eruption in the NW quadrant of the Earth-facing disk best seen in GOES SUVI 304 approximately centered around N45W60. The filament can be seen lifting off the disk as early as 2026-07-21T05:00Z. The filament eruption is followed by a wide-spread area of dimming best seen in SDO AIA 195. This CME follows and partially overlaps with the back of large, far-sided CME: 2026-07-21T06:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 and visible, on-disk source location.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery, and is faint but may be seen to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source may be related to an eruption/brightening from Active Region 14493 (N10W05) starting around 2026-07-21T12:00Z seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. There is a coronal hole north and south of this eruption site which may account for deflection from the on-disk source location.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative measurement based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2 and a faint leading edge seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. It is unclear if the feature visible in SOHO LASCO imagery is outflow or the same event that is seen clearly in STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: Slow moving, possible streamer blowout CME to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 (before data gap), GOES CCOR-1, and to the S in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is currently not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 due to the on going expected data gap due to downlink schedule. The source may be associated with moving/opening field lines in the SW quadrant below a coronal hole and between the longitudes of roughly W20 to W45 and latitudes of roughly S40 to S50 as seen in SDO/AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-21T21:00Z. A dimming signature is also visible to the SW starting around 2026-07-22T01:28Z. There is an additional dimming and brightening starting around 2026-07-22T11:00Z further to the S in SDO/AIA 193. All of these dimming features are believed to be associated with the overall streamer blowout feature to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement using GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 frames. There is likely deflection within the field of view due to proximity of a coronal hole.

cmes.note: Very faint front first seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-07-23T06:36Z. It is also seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SSE in STEREO A COR2. There is some movement and brightening along a filament channel that was centered around S10W00 best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-23T05:54Z. This would require some significant southward deflection, but that could be accounted for by the proximity to a coronal hole south of AR 14493.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. There is some degree of uncertainty in this measurement due to the faintness of the leading edge.

cmes.note: Faint, narrow (<10 degree half-width) CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-23T10:36Z. It is also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. A possible source candidate is some very minor field line movement from beyond the SW limb best seen in SDO AIA 193 as early as 2026-07-23T08:27Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the E in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-07-23T15:38Z. The CME is also visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C3, but not clearly visible in SOHO LASCO C2 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery due to it's faintness. The source is most likely related to a C2.7 flare from around S20E19. The flare and associated eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 131. Field line movement and a faint EUV wave can be seen in SDO AIA 193. The eruption appears to be directed northward.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit of features seen in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C3.

cmes.note: Faint CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely a filament eruption visible beyond the NE limb in SDO/AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 304 and 284 starting around 2026-07-23T14:17Z. The source is also visible to the NW in STEREO A EUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the SE in STEREO A COR2 starting around 2026-07-24T04:38Z. It is also seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is a filament eruption centered around S20E15 best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting as early as 2026-07-24T04:04Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the brightest part of the leading edge based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.
SHOCK measurement tracking the outermost faint feature, based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: Wide CME with irregularly shaped leading edge first seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-7-24T12:48Z. It is also seen to the SE in GOES CCOR-1 and to the SW in STEREO A COR2. In real time, only the earliest frame in seen by SOHO LASCO C2 due to a real-time gap between downlinks. The source is most like a wide opening of field lines best seen beyond the SE limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-07-24T12:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

cmes.note: Faint CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is not directly clear but triangulates well to ~S26E65. Potential weak sources are field line movement over the SE limb in GOES SUVI 171 starting around 2026-07-24T20:20Z, a brightening and field line movement in SDO AIA 171 around ~S04E30 near AR 14494 starting around 2026-07-24T21:01Z (requiring large deflection), or a small brightening in SDO AIA 193 around ~S40E70 starting around 2026-07-24T21:12Z (although this starts right with the front visibility).

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

cmes.note: Faint, diffuse CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and possibly to the N in STEREO A COR2 imagery. This CME is not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This CME is likely associated with moving/opening field lines visible beyond the NE limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-07-24T23:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 frames.

cmes.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely a small brightening and field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193/304 centered around S28W50 starting around 2026-07-25T01:06Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 only 3D measurement using W50 as estimated source longitude, and parameters could vary slightly as a result.

cmes.note: Faint CME observed to the SE only in GOES CCOR-1. No distinct source for this CME is observed with three weak, faint eruptive candidates: field line movement over the E limb in GOES SUVI 171 around 2026-07-25T02:16Z, field line movement over the SSE limb in SDO AIA 171 starting around 2026-07-25T03:03Z, or a brightening south of AR 14494 around S20E35 starting around 2026-07-25T03:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 plane-of-sky.

cmes.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 before a data gap, and in GOES CCOR-1 very faintly. The source is likely AR 14493, with a swath of brightening in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-25T02:28Z centered ~N10W55, with the brightest and most eruptive activity (filament material jostles but poorly erupts if at all) centered ~N05W65.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 only 3D measurement using W65 as the source longitude, as such parameters may vary slightly.

cmes.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in only STEREO A COR2. The source may be an area of slow dimming centered around N50W30 in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-25T03:33Z, offset significantly from the start time due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 not becoming available until 2026-07-25T07:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only 3D measurement using W30 as the approximate source, finding southward deflection (somewhat speculative due to the large deflection necessary here), as such parameters could vary.

cmes.note: Faint CME observed to the SE only in GOES CCOR-1. No distinct source for this CME is observed with two weak, faint eruptive candidates: field line movement over the E limb in SDO AIA 171 starting around 2026-07-25T05:29Z, or a brightening south of AR 14494 around S20E32 starting around 2026-07-25T05:56Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 plane-of-sky.

cmes.note: CME observed to the NW only in GOES CCOR-1, and no distinct source is observed for this CME. In close timing there is a snappy field line movement over the NW limb starting around 2026-07-25T12:36Z in SDO AIA 171/193, but this occurs after the CME is first visible in GOES CCOR-1 and is not a great association.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 plane-of-sky.

cmes.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, very faintly in GOES CCOR-1 and LASCO C3, and likely not in STEREO A COR2. This CME has no clear observed source, and is analyzed to be separate from the source for CME: 2026-07-26T16:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only plane-of-sky as the best observing coronagraph, with the leading edge diffusing within the C2 field-of-view.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the E in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-07-26T16:23Z. It is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 and is covered by a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source of this CME is likely associated with an impulsive M3.2 flare from AR 14494 (S05E03) that peaked at 2026-06-27T15:28Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Highly speculative measurement based on visible source location and three frames in STEREO A COR2. After the third frame, the COR2A imagery becomes too grainy to track the leading edge.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-26T20:26Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is missed in real time by a data gap in STEREO A COR2. The source is like a wide opening of field lines from beyond the NE limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 starting as early as 2026-07-26T18:44Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated, triangulated measurement including new imagery from STEREO A COR2.

Plane-of-sky measurement based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to far-sided source and lack of real-time STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: CME observed to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and faintly in GOES CCOR-1, not in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a real-time downlink gap. The source is a heavily deflected filament eruption observed well in GOES SUVI 304, from a small filament spanning approx. N16E12 to N25W00 (centered N25E05) at 2026-07-27T03:13Z when it began to slowly lift off, more eruptively past 2026-07-27T05:00Z, clearly deflecting sharply NE in the field-of-view. Also observed field line movement and brightening in GOES SUVI 171 and dimming in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and the faint leading edge in GOES CCOR-1.

cmes.note: CME observed to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2, not yet in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a downlink gap. The source is a filament eruption far-sided from Earth, observed first in GOES SUVI 304 as the filament eruption over the NW limb starting around 2026-07-27T05:13Z. STEREO A EUVI 195/304 also observes the eruption site after a data gap ends at 2026-07-27T07:05Z and 2026-07-27T07:15Z respectively, as dimming, double-ribbon flare, and post eruptive arcade centered approximately around N25W125.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

cmes.note: CME visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery in real-time due to a data gap starting at 2026-07-27T06:48Z. The potential source is field line movement on or just beyond the NE limb as seen in SDO AIA 171 imagery in ISWA, SDO AIA 193, and GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-07-27T09:37Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as potential source location near the east limb.

cmes.note: CME visible to the NNE in STEREO A COR2 imagery only. There is a downlink data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time starting at 2026-07-27T06:48Z and the CME is likely obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source is an eruption with dimming seen centered around N45W40 starting as early as 2026-07-27T09:25Z. The eruption is best seen in the NE quadrant of STEREO A EUV 195 imagery and the NW quadrant of SDO AIA 193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the potential source location using STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

cmes.note: Faint CME observed to the SW only in GOES CCOR-1, likely too faint or blocked by occulting disk in STEREO A COR2, and with a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source is likely just south of AR 14491 (S11W79), as a brightening and field line movement centered ~S19W80 in SDO AIA 171/193/304 starting around 2026-07-27T13:28Z and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 starting around 2026-07-27T13:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: 3D GOES CCOR-1 only analysis using W80 as approximate longitude via SDO observations, and as such parameters may vary slightly.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to eruptive activity from a currently unnumbered region centered near N12E80. Subsequent field line movement is visible over the northeast limb starting around 2026-07-27T14:00Z seen in SDO AIA 171 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption from a currently unnumbered region centered near N16E80 starting around 2026-07-27T14:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 171/193/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap starting at 2026-07-27T16:23Z. The source is likely far-sided as there are no clear source signatures visible on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is an eruption near the northeast limb centered near N20E90 starting around 2026-07-27T23:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 131/171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is an eruption from Active Region 14494 (centered near S04W16) starting around 2026-07-27T23:45Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/294/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
